audit_items.title: Verify Consensus Layer correctly obtains active validator indices for epoch-based proposer selection

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The ActiveValidatorIndices function correctly implements the spec's get_active_validator_indices. It iterates through all validators and filters them using IsActiveValidatorUsingTrie which checks: activationEpoch <= epoch && epoch < exitEpoch. This matches the specification requirement for validator activation and exit epoch checks.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The implementation at beacon-chain/core/helpers/validators.go:104-145 correctly filters validators by checking activation_epoch <= epoch < exit_epoch via the checkValidatorActiveStatus helper at line 59.
edge_cases_identified: Validators activating at current epoch are correctly included
Validators exiting at current epoch are correctly excluded
Slashed validators remain in active set (per spec - slashing doesn't affect is_active_validator)

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The invariant that only validators with activation_epoch <= epoch < exit_epoch are included is correctly enforced. The function uses caching via committeeCache for performance but the underlying logic is spec-compliant.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Epoch boundaries are correctly handled. The function accepts any epoch parameter and correctly evaluates validator status at that specific epoch.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - This is an internal function with no external input. The epoch parameter is derived from beacon state, not user input.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code review confirms the implementation matches spec. The checkValidatorActiveStatus function at line 59 correctly implements 'activationEpoch <= epoch && epoch < exitEpoch'. Test coverage exists in validators_test.go:420-578.

audit_items.title: Verify Validator actor cannot influence proposer selection to include inactive validators

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Validator-controlled inputs (attestations, block proposals) do not directly flow into the active validator filtering logic. The active validator set is determined solely by the beacon state's validator registry, which is updated through deterministic state transitions.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Active validator computation is deterministic based on state and epoch, with no validator-controllable parameters.
edge_cases_identified: State transitions updating validator status are processed before proposer computation in epoch processing

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The separation of concerns is maintained: validators submit attestations/proposals, but the active set computation uses only finalized state data.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: No race conditions identified between validator status updates and proposer calculations due to sequential epoch processing.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - No validator input can affect the active validator filtering algorithm.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The active validator index computation is purely state-derived with no validator-controllable inputs. The epoch processing ensures validator registry updates complete before proposer lookahead computation.

audit_items.title: Can IGNORED sidecars be permanently discarded or forwarded without re-validation?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The validation function returns pubsub.ValidationIgnore for conditions like future slot (line 91) and parent not seen (line 99-112). When IGNORE is returned, the message is NOT forwarded to peers. For parent-not-seen cases, an async request is triggered to fetch the parent block.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - IGNORED sidecars are not forwarded (pubsub library behavior), and the code handles reprocessing via async parent block fetching.
edge_cases_identified: Future slot sidecars are simply ignored without explicit queuing
Parent-not-seen sidecars trigger async parent fetch but the sidecar itself may be dropped if parent arrives later

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The pubsub.ValidationIgnore status prevents message forwarding per libp2p pubsub semantics. However, there's no explicit queue for IGNORED sidecars - they rely on re-gossip or re-request.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: The IGNORE queue is implicit in the pubsub layer, not explicitly managed by Prysm.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Medium - Flooding with far-future sidecars could consume resources, but pubsub's built-in message cache provides some protection.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: IGNORED sidecars are not forwarded (correct). However, explicit re-validation queuing is not implemented - the node relies on re-gossip. For parent-not-seen cases, only the parent is fetched async, not the sidecar re-validated.
recommendations: Consider explicit queuing mechanism for IGNORED sidecars pending parent blocks
Add metrics for IGNORE conditions to monitor potential issues

edge_cases_identified: Domain separation ensures proposer selection is independent from attester/sync committee selection

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: DomainBeaconProposer (0x00000000) is distinct from DomainBeaconAttester (0x01000000) and other domains as seen in mainnet_config.go:163-175.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: All domain constants are immutable compile-time values with no runtime modification possible.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - Domain constants are hardcoded and match Ethereum consensus specifications.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code at beacon-chain/core/helpers/validators.go:269 shows proper domain usage. Domain constants at config/params/mainnet_config.go:163-175 are correctly defined and unique.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: All DOMAIN_* constants at config/params/mainnet_config.go:163-175 have unique values that match the Ethereum consensus specification exactly.

audit_items.title: Can process_epoch sub-process execution order be violated, causing state divergence across clients?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: ProcessEpoch in fulu/transition.go first calls electra.ProcessEpoch (which contains the 15 standard epoch processing steps in order) and then calls ProcessProposerLookahead as step 16. The ordering is enforced by sequential function calls.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The implementation follows the specification's required ordering: 15 standard steps via electra.ProcessEpoch, then process_proposer_lookahead as step 16.
edge_cases_identified: No async or parallel execution - all steps are synchronous and sequential

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The epoch processing is strictly sequential with no possibility of reordering. Error handling ensures early termination if any step fails.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: ProcessProposerLookahead executes only after electra.ProcessEpoch returns successfully.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - Execution order is enforced by synchronous function calls with no external control.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code at beacon-chain/core/fulu/transition.go:14-20 shows strictly sequential execution: electra.ProcessEpoch() followed by ProcessProposerLookahead(). No concurrent access patterns exist.

audit_items.title: Can process_proposer_lookahead execute before all 15 preceding steps in process_epoch complete?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: ProcessProposerLookahead is called only after electra.ProcessEpoch returns (line 19). If electra.ProcessEpoch returns an error, ProcessProposerLookahead is never called.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The function is guaranteed to execute as step 16 after all 15 prior steps complete.
edge_cases_identified: Error handling ensures ProcessProposerLookahead only runs on successful completion of prior steps

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The ordering invariant is maintained through synchronous function calls and error propagation.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: No conditional branches or early returns bypass the ordering.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - No external input can affect execution ordering.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The code structure at fulu/transition.go:14-20 guarantees ProcessProposerLookahead executes only after electra.ProcessEpoch completes successfully. This is enforced by Go's sequential execution model.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Is the proposer_lookahead shift operation correctly removing exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: At line 35: copy(lookAhead[:lastEpochStart], lookAhead[params.BeaconConfig().SlotsPerEpoch:]). The lastEpochStart is computed as len(lookAhead) - SlotsPerEpoch. This shifts the array by exactly SlotsPerEpoch slots.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The shift operation correctly uses SlotsPerEpoch as the offset, removing exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries from the front.
edge_cases_identified: The shift amount is SlotsPerEpoch, not SlotsPerEpoch-1 or SlotsPerEpoch+1

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The copy operation shifts the array left by exactly SlotsPerEpoch positions, then new proposers are appended to fill the last epoch.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: lastEpochStart = len(lookAhead) - SlotsPerEpoch ensures correct array slicing.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - SlotsPerEpoch is a configuration constant.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Line 35 correctly shifts by SlotsPerEpoch. The copy operation at line 35 and new proposer assignment at line 43 maintain the correct lookahead array structure.

audit_items.title: Verify Consensus Layer proposer_lookahead state consistency during epoch transitions

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The proposer_lookahead array length is maintained by the shift-then-fill pattern: old entries are shifted out, new epoch entries are computed and filled in. The final SetProposerLookahead call updates the state.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The lookahead array maintains consistent length across epoch transitions.
edge_cases_identified: First epoch and post-finalization edge cases are handled by the underlying state management

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Array length remains EPOCHS_AHEAD * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH after each transition due to the balanced shift-and-fill operation.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: The shift amount equals the fill amount, maintaining array size.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - State consistency is enforced by the deterministic algorithm.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The implementation maintains lookahead array consistency by removing exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries and adding exactly SLOTS_PER_EPOCH new entries.

audit_items.title: Verify Validator receives correct proposer assignments after lookahead shift

phase1_findings.code_behavior: After the shift, the lookahead array contains proposer indices for the upcoming epochs. Validators query this array to determine their proposal duties.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The lookahead array is correctly maintained for validator duty queries.

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The array indices map directly to slot offsets from the current epoch start.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Array indexing is straightforward with no off-by-one potential.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - The array structure is deterministic and consistent.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The proposer lookahead array is correctly maintained, ensuring validators receive accurate proposer assignments.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is the sidecar subnet validation correctly enforced in the gossip validation pipeline?

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Does the gossip validation pipeline correctly IGNORE (not REJECT) sidecars with future slots?

Add monitoring for IGNORE-related resource consumption

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Line 40 initializes maxRequestDataColumnSidecars from beaconConfig.MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars. The quota is decremented with each sidecar written and streaming stops when quota reaches 0 (lines 97-105).
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS is enforced as an absolute cap.
edge_cases_identified: Quota is checked per sidecar, not per batch

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The quota mechanism ensures no more than MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars are returned.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Streaming terminates when quota reaches 0.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Resource exhaustion is prevented by the quota.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code at rpc_data_column_sidecars_by_range.go:40-105 correctly enforces MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS limit.

audit_items.title: Does the beacon node (actor-beacon-node) correctly enforce sidecar count limits before streaming responses to P2P clients?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The streamDataColumnBatch function checks quota before each write and stops when quota is exhausted. The limit is checked during streaming, not before.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Limit is enforced during streaming with early termination.
edge_cases_identified: Streaming stops mid-batch if quota exhausted

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The quota mechanism provides real-time enforcement during streaming.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Partial batches may be returned if quota is reached mid-batch.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - No over-serving possible due to quota check per sidecar.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The quota mechanism at streamDataColumnBatch correctly limits total sidecars returned.

audit_items.title: Does the request-response client (actor-req-resp-client) validate that received responses do not exceed expected sidecar limits?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The client validates received sidecars via isSidecarSlotWithinBounds and isSidecarIndexRequested. There's also a check at line 46 for errMaxResponseDataColumnSidecarsExceeded.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Client-side validation prevents accepting excess sidecars.
edge_cases_identified: Excess responses trigger connection termination

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Client validates response count against expectations.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Malicious peers sending excess data are detected and handled.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Client-side validation provides defense in depth.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Client at rpc_send_request.go validates response sizes and errors on excess.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange response enforce strict (slot, column_index) ordering?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Line 85-90 sorts requested columns. The response iterates blocks in slot order (from batcher) and columns in sorted order. This provides (slot, column_index) ordering.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Response ordering follows specification.
edge_cases_identified: Column sorting ensures consistent ordering within slots

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The iteration pattern (blocks by slot, then columns sorted) ensures correct ordering.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Empty or single-item responses trivially satisfy ordering.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - Ordering is server-controlled.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code at lines 85-90 (slices.Sort) and iteration pattern ensure (slot, column_index) ordering.

audit_items.title: Does the beacon node's DataColumnSidecarsByRange handler guarantee post-condition ordering before transmission?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Columns are sorted before iteration (line 85-90). Blocks are processed in slot order from the batcher. Combined, this guarantees ordering.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Ordering is guaranteed by code structure.
edge_cases_identified: No race conditions possible in single-threaded streaming

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The deterministic iteration pattern guarantees ordering.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: All edge cases (empty, single, full) maintain ordering.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - Server-side ordering is deterministic.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The code structure guarantees (slot, column_index) ordering in responses.

audit_items.title: Does the requesting client validate or tolerate ordering violations in DataColumnSidecarsByRange responses?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The client validates slot bounds and column indices but does not explicitly validate ordering. It relies on server compliance.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - No explicit ordering validation on client side.
edge_cases_identified: Out-of-order responses would be accepted if otherwise valid

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Client trusts server for ordering; no explicit check exists.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Out-of-order data would not cause crashes but might affect processing efficiency.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Processing handles unordered data gracefully.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Client does not explicitly validate ordering but handles unordered data without crashes.
recommendations: Consider adding client-side ordering validation for defense in depth

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRange abort response streaming when fork choice changes during an active request?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The handler uses a context with timeout (line 36) and the batcher checks context cancellation. However, no explicit fork choice change detection during streaming is visible.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - Context cancellation exists but explicit fork choice abort is not implemented.
edge_cases_identified: Reorgs during streaming may result in stale data being served

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The IsCanonical check in batcher filters non-canonical blocks, but this is evaluated at batch creation time.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Fork choice changes after batch creation could include stale data.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Medium - Stale fork data could be served during reorgs.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: IsCanonical filtering exists but is not continuously re-evaluated during streaming. Fork choice changes during streaming may not abort the response.
recommendations: Consider implementing fork choice change notification to abort active streaming responses

audit_items.title: Does the beacon node correctly track fork choice state during DataColumnSidecarsByRange streaming and propagate changes to active handlers?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The handler receives IsCanonical function reference but does not subscribe to fork choice updates during streaming.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - Fork choice tracking is snapshot-based, not continuous.
edge_cases_identified: No notification mechanism for mid-stream fork choice changes

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Fork choice state is checked at batch creation, not continuously.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Reorgs happening after batch creation are not detected.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Medium - Race window exists for serving stale data.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: No continuous fork choice tracking during streaming. Snapshot-based approach has race condition potential.
recommendations: Implement fork choice update subscription for active streaming handlers

audit_items.title: Can an attacker exploit timing of DataColumnSidecarsByRange requests during reorgs to receive stale fork data?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: An attacker timing requests during reorgs could potentially receive data from the pre-reorg chain if the streaming began before the reorg completed.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - The race window exists but practical exploitation is difficult.
edge_cases_identified: Timing attack requires precise coordination with reorg events

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The attack window is small but non-zero.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Practical exploitation requires significant network control.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low to Medium - Timing attack is theoretically possible but practically difficult.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Theoretical timing attack vector exists but practical exploitation is challenging. Client-side validation provides some protection.
recommendations: Document the timing window
Consider fork choice notification for defense in depth

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot compute total requested_columns_count across ALL identifiers before validating against MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Lines 142-155 show validateDataColumnsByRootRequest computes total = sum(len(id.Columns) for all identifiers) and checks if total > MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Total count across ALL identifiers is computed before validation.
edge_cases_identified: The aggregation correctly sums across all identifiers

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The total count is computed by iterating all identifiers and summing column counts.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Validation occurs BEFORE any processing.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - The aggregation prevents the distributed column attack.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code at rpc_data_column_sidecars_by_root.go:142-155 correctly aggregates across all identifiers and validates against MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS.

audit_items.title: Does the beacon node (actor-beacon-node) properly reject P2P requests where aggregated column count exceeds MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Lines 48-53 call validateDataColumnsByRootRequest and on error, downscore the peer and write error response, then return error.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Validation occurs before processing with proper rejection.
edge_cases_identified: Peer is downscored on validation failure

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Validation is synchronous and blocking, occurring before any data retrieval.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Rejection is atomic - no partial processing occurs.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Early rejection prevents resource consumption.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code at lines 48-53 properly rejects and downscores peers exceeding the limit.

audit_items.title: Can a malicious req-resp client (actor-req-resp-client) bypass the column count limit by distributing requests across multiple identifiers?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The validation sums across ALL identifiers, so distributing columns across identifiers does not bypass the limit.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - The aggregation prevents the bypass attack.
edge_cases_identified: 1000 identifiers with 1 column each would total 1000, correctly exceeding limits

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The aggregation is complete and correct.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Any distribution pattern is correctly summed.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - The bypass attack is prevented by proper aggregation.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The validation at lines 142-155 correctly prevents the distributed column bypass attack.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Is the minimum_request_epoch correctly computed and enforced for DataColumnSidecarsByRoot requests?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Lines 79-82 compute minReqSlot using dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot(). Lines 121-127 filter out sidecars older than minReqSlot.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - minimum_request_epoch is correctly computed and enforced.
edge_cases_identified: Old sidecars are silently filtered, not rejected

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The minimum epoch computation matches the specification: max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH).
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Edge cases near fork epoch are handled correctly.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Old data requests are filtered, not served.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Code correctly computes and enforces minimum epoch at lines 79-82 and 121-127.

audit_items.title: Does the Beacon Node correctly reject DataColumnSidecarsByRoot requests for epochs before FULU_FORK_EPOCH?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The dataColumnsRPCMinValidSlot function returns FuluForkEpoch as the minimum when current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS is less than FuluForkEpoch.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Pre-fork epoch requests are filtered by the minimum slot check.
edge_cases_identified: Sidecars from pre-fork are not served

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The max() operation ensures FULU_FORK_EPOCH is the absolute minimum.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Pre-fork requests result in empty or filtered responses.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - Pre-fork data cannot be requested.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The minimum epoch computation at lines 175-183 correctly uses max() to enforce FULU_FORK_EPOCH minimum.

audit_items.title: Is the request-response client properly validating epoch bounds before forwarding DataColumnSidecarsByRoot requests?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The client validates request size (lines 612-625) but does not explicitly validate epoch bounds. Epoch validation is handled server-side.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - Client validates count but relies on server for epoch validation.
edge_cases_identified: Client trusts server for epoch-related filtering

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Epoch validation is server-side responsibility per the current implementation.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Invalid epoch requests would receive empty or filtered responses.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Server-side validation provides protection.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Client relies on server-side epoch validation, which is correctly implemented.
recommendations: Consider client-side epoch validation as defense in depth

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot reject requests for sidecars of blocks that failed gossip validation?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The handler retrieves sidecars from dataColumnStorage.Get() which only returns verified sidecars. Invalid/failed blocks are not stored, so their sidecars cannot be retrieved.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Only verified sidecars are stored and served.
edge_cases_identified: Storage only contains sidecars that passed validation

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The storage layer only persists sidecars that passed all validation checks.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Failed validation prevents storage, which prevents serving.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - Invalid sidecars are not stored.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The storage model ensures only validated sidecars can be retrieved and served.

audit_items.title: Does the beacon node maintain accurate gossip validation state to prevent serving invalid sidecars?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Validation state is implicit in storage: only validated sidecars are stored. There's no separate validation state tracking.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: COMPLIANT - Storage-based approach maintains validation state.
edge_cases_identified: No race conditions between validation and storage

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Validation is complete before storage, ensuring only valid sidecars are persisted.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Atomic validation-then-storage prevents inconsistent states.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: None - The storage model prevents serving invalid data.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The validation-before-storage pattern ensures only valid sidecars are served.

audit_items.title: Can a malicious request-response client exploit timing or response patterns to determine block existence in the database?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The response returns whatever sidecars are found. Missing sidecars result in empty response for that identifier. Timing differences might exist between found/not-found cases.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - Some information leakage may occur via timing or response size.
edge_cases_identified: Timing side-channel for block existence is possible

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: Response patterns may reveal block existence information.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Empty vs non-empty responses leak information.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Low - Information disclosure about block existence, not security-critical data.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: Minor information leakage about block existence is possible but not security-critical. This is inherent to the protocol design.
recommendations: Document the information disclosure as expected behavior

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-007/tb-008: Is blob data from EL via engine_getBlobsV2 validated before conversion to data columns?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: The engine_getBlobsV2 data flow needs specific code path verification. EL is trusted due to JWT authentication and co-location assumption per spec.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: REQUIRES-REVIEW - The trust boundary assumption needs verification.
edge_cases_identified: Compromised EL could potentially inject invalid blobs

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The spec documents trust in EL due to JWT authentication.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: Defense in depth for EL data is not mandated by spec.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: Medium if EL is compromised, but out of scope per trust model.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: The engine_getBlobsV2 data flow requires specific code path analysis to verify trust boundary handling.
recommendations: Verify EL data handling code path
Consider optional KZG verification for defense in depth

audit_items.title: Does the beacon node implement defense-in-depth for blob data integrity despite JWT-authenticated EL trust assumption?

phase1_findings.code_behavior: Defense in depth for EL-sourced blobs is not visible in the reviewed code. The trust assumption is per specification.
phase1_findings.specification_compliance: PARTIAL - No visible defense in depth for EL data.
edge_cases_identified: Compromised EL could inject invalid data that gets gossiped

phase2_findings.invariant_analysis: The spec trusts EL, so defense in depth is optional.
phase2_findings.boundary_conditions: JWT compromise would break the security model.
phase2_findings.attack_surface: High if JWT is compromised, but this is acknowledged in spec.

phase3_findings.evidence_summary: No explicit defense in depth for EL-sourced data. Per spec, this is acceptable under the trust model.
recommendations: Document the EL trust assumption clearly
Consider optional KZG verification flag for high-security deployments
